prompt: Which part of a provisioned Redshift cluster does an SQL client connect to?
hint: One part plans the query and gathers the answers.

choices.text: Each compute node, in turn
choices.why: The compute nodes take their work from the leader; a client never talks to them.

choices.text: The leader node
choices.why: Right. It parses, plans and compiles the SQL, and gathers what the slices return.

choices.text: The slice that holds the rows the query wants
choices.why: Every slice holds a share of every table, and only the leader knows how to combine them.

choices.text: Redshift Managed Storage, in S3
choices.why: Managed storage holds the blocks; it answers no SQL.

prompt: A query reads three columns of a twenty-column table. What does columnar storage save it?
hint: Each column is written in blocks of its own.

choices.text: Nothing, since Redshift reads whole rows and drops the unwanted columns afterwards
choices.why: That is how a row store reads; Redshift writes each column apart precisely to avoid it.

choices.text: It reads the three columns from the leader's memory
choices.why: The leader holds no table data; the slices read the blocks.

choices.text: The blocks of the other seventeen columns
choices.why: Right. Only the three columns' blocks are read; the rest stay on disk.

choices.text: It reads every column, but each one compressed
choices.why: Compression is real and is a second saving; the first is not reading the other columns at all.

prompt: Through moto, `get-statement-result` answers a `SELECT` on a table nobody created with three rows holding a street and a city. What does that show?
hint: Was there ever a table called `orders`?

choices.text: That Redshift fills a new database with sample rows
choices.why: A new Redshift database is empty, and the query would fail naming the missing table.

choices.text: That a table called `orders` already existed in the cluster
choices.why: There is no cluster to hold one; and the rows have no date and no count, which the query asked for.

choices.text: That moto hands back its own sample answer and runs no SQL
choices.why: Right. The same three rows come back whatever the statement says.

choices.text: That the Data API cached the result of another account's query
choices.why: Nothing is shared between accounts; moto imitates one account and invents the rows.

prompt: An RA3 cluster grows from two nodes to three. Which of these change? Choose all that apply.
hint: Compute and storage are priced apart on RA3.

choices.text: The number of slices sharing each query's work
choices.why: Yes. Each `ra3.xlplus` node brings two more.

choices.text: The hourly compute price of the cluster
choices.why: Yes. Nodes are billed per node-hour.

choices.text: The amount of data the cluster stores
choices.why: The data is in managed storage, and adding compute does not change it.

choices.text: The price per GB-month of managed storage
choices.why: That is a separate line of the sheet, 0.043, whatever the node count.

prompt: Match each distribution style to the table it suits.
hint: One of the right-hand options is about sort keys.

pairs.right: Any table, until you know its joins better than the statistics do
A large table with no dominant join
Two large tables joined on one column
A small table every report joins

right_distractors: A table filtered mostly by date ranges

prompt: A model puts 10,000 rows on 4 slices and the fullest slice gets 6,000 of them. What is its ratio to the mean, the `max/mean` that `slices.py` prints? Give two decimal places.
hint: The mean is the rows divided by the slices.

prompt: To avoid the skew `c-01` causes, Quitanda keys `orders` on `order_id` and keeps `customers` keyed on `customer_id`. What does a join of the two on `customer_id` now cost?
hint: An order sits next to its customer only if both hashed to the same slice.

choices.text: Nothing extra, because both tables are `KEY`-distributed
choices.why: They are keyed on different columns, so matching rows rarely share a slice.

choices.text: About three rows in four move to another slice before the join runs
choices.why: Right. The model moved 7,449 of 10,000, what a hash that ignores the join column gives with four slices.

choices.text: The skew moves to `customers`, which now holds `c-01`'s orders
choices.why: `customers` holds one row for `c-01`; orders are not stored in it.

choices.text: The join is refused until both tables share a key
choices.why: Redshift runs any join; a mismatch costs movement, not an error.

prompt: Why is `stores` declared `DISTSTYLE ALL` in `orders.sql`?
hint: How big is it, and who joins it?

choices.text: `ALL` keeps its rows sorted by `store_id`
choices.why: Order is the sort key's job; `ALL` is about where the rows live.

choices.text: It is tiny and every report joins it, so a copy on each node means no join with it moves a row
choices.why: Right. The cost, a write per node on every load, is nothing at forty rows.

choices.text: A `SMALLINT` key column requires `ALL`
choices.why: The type of a column does not dictate the style.

choices.text: `ALL` deals its rows out evenly across the slices
choices.why: That is `EVEN`. `ALL` puts a full copy on every node.

prompt: `orders` has `COMPOUND SORTKEY (dt, customer_id)`. Which of these filters lets the zone maps skip the most blocks?
hint: Look at the first column of the key, and at what `zonemaps.py` printed.

choices.text: `customer_id = 'c-17'`
choices.why: The second column helps only within each value of the first; the model read 36 of 40 blocks.
Right. A filter on the leading column read 2 of 40 blocks in the model.

choices.text: Both equally, since both columns are in the key
choices.why: Equal weight is what an interleaved key aims at; a compound key favours its first column.

choices.text: Neither, because zone maps need an index
choices.why: Zone maps are kept for every block and need no index; they need sorted rows.

prompt: Why is an interleaved sort key a poor fit for Quitanda's `orders` table?
hint: What do the values of `dt` do over time?

choices.text: An interleaved key can hold one column, and `orders` needs two
choices.why: It holds several columns and weighs them equally; that is its whole point.

choices.text: Interleaved keys cannot be combined with `DISTKEY`
choices.why: Distribution and sort order are independent choices.

choices.text: `dt` only ever grows, so new rows crowd into one corner of the order and the table keeps needing an expensive `VACUUM REINDEX`
choices.why: Right. AWS's documentation advises against interleaving a date or an identity column.

choices.text: Interleaved keys sort only the unsorted region at the end
choices.why: The unsorted region exists under any sort key; it is not what interleaving changes.

prompt: The smallest and largest value of a column in each block, kept in memory so a filter can skip the block, is that block's zone ___.
hint: Two words, the first already given.

prompt: In Redshift Serverless, what does the namespace hold?
hint: One of the two things is what the warehouse is, the other what it runs on.

choices.text: The capacity in RPUs and the network it sits in
choices.why: That is the workgroup.

choices.text: The history of the queries that have run
choices.why: Neither name is for history; the namespace is the data and who may use it.

choices.text: The compute nodes and their slices
choices.why: Serverless has no nodes for you to see; capacity is in RPUs, and it is the workgroup's.

choices.text: The databases, tables, users and their storage
choices.why: Right. A workgroup can be replaced and the namespace's data does not move.

prompt: A Serverless workgroup has a base capacity of 8 RPUs, and no query ran between 22:00 and 07:00. What did those nine hours cost in compute?
hint: When is an RPU-hour billed?

choices.text: 8 RPUs × 9 hours at the RPU-hour price
choices.why: The base is what a query starts with, not a charge for existing.

choices.text: Nothing, as compute is billed only while queries run
choices.why: Right. Storage is still billed, at the managed storage rate.

choices.text: 128 RPUs × 9 hours, the default base
choices.why: The base was set to 8, and no base is billed while idle.

choices.text: One minute for each hour, the 60-second minimum
choices.why: The minimum applies each time compute starts, and it never started.

prompt: Which Serverless setting keeps an expensive query from running up an expensive month?
hint: Redshift scales above the base while a heavy query runs.

choices.text: The base capacity
choices.why: The base is where a query starts; Redshift scales above it.

choices.text: The maximum capacity
choices.why: Right. It is the ceiling on how far Redshift scales.

choices.text: The namespace's storage quota
choices.why: Storage is a small line; the RPU-hours are what an expensive query runs up.

choices.text: The 60-second minimum per start
choices.why: That is a billing rule, not a setting, and it sets a floor rather than a ceiling.

prompt: By the sheet, an `ra3.xlplus` node costs 1.731 USD an hour. What is the compute of a three-node cluster for a 30-day month of 720 hours, in USD? Give two decimal places.
hint: Nodes × price × hours.

prompt: Quitanda's analysts now work 6 hours a day at 32 RPUs. In a 30-day month, which costs less in compute: Serverless, or the two-node `ra3.xlplus` cluster at 2,492.64 USD?
hint: An hour at 32 RPUs is 19.1232 USD.

choices.text: Serverless, which bills only the hours that are used
choices.why: It does, and six of them a day come to 3,442.18 USD, above the cluster.

choices.text: They come to the same, because both bill by the hour
choices.why: They bill different hours: the cluster every hour it exists, Serverless every hour it works.

choices.text: The cluster
choices.why: Right. 19.1232 × 6 × 30 is 3,442.18 USD; the line falls at about 4.34 hours a day.

choices.text: Serverless, because storage is cheaper there
choices.why: Storage is 0.043 per GB-month in both, so it does not move the line.

prompt: A Redshift Spectrum query scans 0.4 TB of files in S3. What does it cost by the sheet?
hint: Spectrum is billed like Athena.

choices.text: 0.24 USD, at the RPU-hour price
choices.why: That multiplies by the Serverless price; Spectrum is billed by the data scanned.

choices.text: 5.00 USD, one TB being the smallest unit billed
choices.why: The price is per TB, and a fraction of a TB costs that fraction.

choices.text: Nothing, since the files are already paid for as S3 storage
choices.why: Storing and scanning are separate charges.

choices.text: 2.00 USD

prompt: Put the life of a query on a provisioned cluster in order.
hint: The leader appears twice.
items: The client sends the SQL to the leader node on port 5439
The leader plans the query and compiles it into code
Every slice scans its share, skipping the blocks its zone maps rule out
The leader gathers what the slices returned and sends the answer

prompt: Since a restaurant chain became a customer, every report on `orders` is slower, and `SVV_TABLE_INFO` shows a high `skew_rows` for it. What is the likeliest cause, and the fix?
hint: `skew_rows` compares the fullest slice with the emptiest.

choices.text: The sort key has gone unsorted; run `VACUUM SORT ONLY`
choices.why: Unsorted rows widen zone maps; they do not put more rows on one slice.

choices.text: The base capacity is too low; raise it
choices.why: Base capacity is Serverless; this is a cluster whose rows are unevenly shared.

choices.text: `DISTKEY (customer_id)` meets one dominant customer; redistribute on a column without one, or `EVEN`
choices.why: Right. One slice holds the chain's orders and every scan waits for it.

choices.text: Spectrum is scanning CSV; convert the files to Parquet
choices.why: `orders` is a table in the warehouse, not files in S3.

prompt: Which of these were measured in this lesson, rather than taken from AWS's documentation? Choose all that apply.
hint: Two things ran: moto, and two Python models.

choices.text: In the model, a key on `customer_id` put 5,420 of 10,000 rows on one slice
choices.why: Yes, `slices.py` printed it.

choices.text: moto leaves a Data API statement `STARTED`
choices.why: Yes, five seconds after it was sent.

choices.text: An `ra3.xlplus` node has two slices
choices.why: That is AWS's documentation; moto runs no nodes to count.

choices.text: `DS_BCAST_INNER` copies a whole table to every node
choices.why: From the documentation of `EXPLAIN`; no plan was produced here.

choices.text: Serverless bills per second with a 60-second minimum
choices.why: Documented by AWS; moto could not even create a namespace.
